sermons.subject: Sunday's Sermon at Grace Life: "Not Guests, Family" (Hebrews 4:14–16)
sermons.title: Not Guests, Family
sermons.church: Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
sermons.body:
Hi Sanqueta,

I wanted to share a summary of the most recent sermon at Grace Life so we can go over it together.

WHAT A SAVIOR, PART 10: NOT GUESTS, FAMILY
Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
Sunday, October 25, 2026
Passage: Hebrews 4:14-16
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2PVsyRkfsbc

"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess. For we do not have a high priest who is unable to empathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who has been tempted in every way, just as we are—yet he did not sin. Let us then approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need." (Hebrews 4:14-16, NIV)

THE BIG IDEA

The pastor opened with something every parent knows. A guest at your house asks where to hang their coat and stays away from closed doors. Our kids walk in, drop their shoes, and find the hidden snacks, because they aren't guests. They're family. A lot of believers relate to God like guests. Some are "striving guests" trying to earn their place. Some are "hiding guests" keeping their distance out of shame. Some are "waiting guests" who haven't come inside yet. Hebrews 4:14-16 says Jesus, our great high priest, has made us family. As he put it: "we view ourselves as guests rather than children, but as followers of Jesus, we've been adopted into God's family."

THE MAIN POINTS

1. We have a great high priest who finished it for us (verse 14).
In the Old Testament, only the high priest could go behind the curtain into God's presence, and the sacrifices never stopped. Jesus offered himself once, for good, and sat down because the work was done.
- "A priest who is still working stands, but a priest who has finished sits. Jesus is sitting. And today if you are a striving guest, trying to earn your place, you can stop."
- "Confession is not despairing. It's declaring. He finished it. And I'm holding fast to him."

2. We have a great high priest who feels it with us (verse 15).
Jesus knows weakness, loneliness, betrayal, and temptation, yet he never sinned. He doesn't just feel sorry for us. He stands with us.
- "See, pity looks down from a distance. But sympathy stands beside you."
- "Jesus is not ashamed of you. The Holy One is not embarrassed to call you brother, sister."
- "He doesn't stand over your mess. Jesus gets down with you in the mess."

3. We have a great high priest who frees us to come (verse 16).
"Confidence" here means the freedom to speak openly without fear. Our access to God rests on Jesus' blood, not on how our week went.
- "Your worst week ever before the Lord does not lower your access to him... And your best week, it also doesn't raise your access to God."
- "When you mess up you run to the throne."

To anyone still waiting outside, he said: "your invitation to come inside was written with Jesus' blood." And from John 1:12: "Not guests, children."

TAKEAWAYS FOR OUR MARRIAGE AND FAMILY

- Serve from rest, not for approval. "Please don't stop serving, but serve from rest. Don't serve for approval." We can love each other and our kids because we're already loved, not to prove ourselves.
- Make our home a place where people can be real. "Feeling at home, it means expressing frustration and fear. It means hugs and tears."
- Show our kids what the Father is like. If a child breaks something, we're upset, but they'd never be put out of the house. Our grace gives them an early picture of God's grace.
- Grace forgives and changes us. "The throne of grace offers help to change, but not permission to compromise."
- Pray like children, not guests. Bring our needs honestly, anytime, anywhere.
- A daily reminder: "Every time you open the door, I want you to look at that door knob. And let it remind you that you are a child of God."

WHAT OTHER TRUSTED TEACHERS SAY

John Piper, "Draw Near to the Throne of Grace with Confidence" (sermon, Desiring God)
Piper says this passage gives two commands: hold fast to our hope, and draw near to God in prayer. He also gives the reasons we can do both. Jesus is alive, in God's presence, and full of sympathy because he was tempted in every way like us and never gave in. That's the same point the sermon made: Jesus feels it with us, so we don't have to hide.
"He does not roll his eyes at your pain or cluck his tongue at your struggle with sin."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/draw-near-to-the-throne-of-grace-with-confidence

John Piper, "Jesus Never Gave In" (sermon, Desiring God)
Here Piper says Jesus is both great and close. He is God above the heavens, and he is also right beside us in every pain and temptation. We need both: his greatness so we can trust him, and his tenderness so we feel free to come to him.
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/jesus-never-gave-in

Billy Graham, "The Throne of Grace" (daily devotion, Billy Graham Evangelistic Association)
Graham says prayer is simply a two-way conversation with God. He points out that many people only pray in a crisis. Hebrews 4:16 invites us to come boldly every day, not just in emergencies. That matches the sermon's call to carry the throne of grace into the hospital elevator and the break room.
"The answers to all our problems can be had through contact with almighty God."
https://billygraham.org/devotions/the-throne-of-grace

Skip Heitzig, "Jesus, Our High Priest and Intercessor" (Decision magazine, Billy Graham Evangelistic Association)
This article explains that Old Testament priests never sat down because their work was never done. The tabernacle didn't even have a chair. Jesus sat down at God's right hand because his sacrifice was complete, and now he prays for us. That's the sermon's first point, "He finished it," from Billy Graham's ministry.
"It's done. It's finished. It's over."
https://billygraham.org/decision-magazine/articles/jesus-our-high-priest-and-intercessor-1

Tony Evans, "Entering God's Rest" (sermon on Hebrews 4:9-16)
Dr. Evans preaches through the verses just before and including our passage. He explains that God's rest is much more than taking a day off. That connects with the sermon's reminder to "serve from rest" and stop striving to earn our place. The full sermon can be heard on his site.
https://go.tonyevans.org/tony-evans-sermons/entering-gods-rest

Love you,

-- 
Sincerely,
Greg

sermons.subject: Sunday's Sermon at Grace Life: "More Than Qualified" (Hebrews 5:1–14)
sermons.title: More Than Qualified
sermons.church: Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
sermons.body:
Hi Sanqueta,

I wanted to share a summary of today's sermon at Grace Life so we can go over it together.

WHAT A SAVIOR, PART 11: MORE THAN QUALIFIED
Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
Sunday, November 1, 2026
Passage: Hebrews 5:1-14
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sp9u-I5s3dk

"Every high priest is selected from among the people and is appointed to represent the people in matters related to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins. He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and are going astray, since he himself is subject to weakness. This is why he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people. And no one takes this honor on himself, but he receives it when called by God, just as Aaron was.

In the same way, Christ did not take on himself the glory of becoming a high priest. But God said to him, 'You are my Son; today I have become your Father.' And he says in another place, 'You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek.'

During the days of Jesus' life on earth, he offered up prayers and petitions with fervent cries and tears to the one who could save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission. Son though he was, he learned obedience from what he suffered and, once made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him and was designated by God to be high priest in the order of Melchizedek.

We have much to say about this, but it is hard to make it clear to you because you no longer try to understand. In fact, though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you the elementary truths of God's word all over again. You need milk, not solid food! Anyone who lives on milk, being still an infant, is not acquainted with the teaching about righteousness. But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained themselves to distinguish good from evil." (Hebrews 5:1-14, NIV)

THE BIG IDEA

Pastor Joel opened with his grandfather's 74-year-old razor. Some old things really are better, but some old things need to go, like worn-out shoes or a bald tire. The first readers of Hebrews were tempted to go back to the old system of priests and animal sacrifices. Hebrews 5 makes the case that Jesus is the better high priest, and the only way to God. He said these chapters answer the question underneath every religion and every guilty conscience: "how can someone like me get to a God like him?" The answer: "only through Jesus. Only through Jesus. He is the only way that we get to God."

THE MAIN POINTS

He said three words sum up what qualified a high priest: "One, selection. Two, sympathy. Three, sacrifice." Jesus doesn't just meet each one. He's more than qualified.

1. Selection: Jesus was chosen by God (verses 1, 4-6).
Nobody voted for the high priest or took the job for himself. God chose Aaron and his line. In the same way, God appointed Jesus, and Jesus is more than his pick.
- "he wasn't just selected by God, he is God's Son."
- "he's not just gonna serve a lifetime, the Bible just said he's gonna serve forever in the order of Melchizedek."

2. Sympathy: Jesus understands us (verses 2, 7-8).
A high priest had to be human so he could understand the people he represented. Jesus prayed "with fervent cries and tears." He knows heartbreak and dread, and on the cross he carried the full weight of our sin, which none of us will ever have to carry.
- "This is why God didn't choose angels to be our high priest. They don't understand us."
- "Jesus suffered in a way that none of us will ever be able to understand."
- "There's nothing that we're gonna go through that he can't say to you, I get it. I sympathize, I understand."

3. Sacrifice: Jesus is the sacrifice (verses 3, 9-10).
The old high priests had to offer sacrifices for their own sins first, over and over. Jesus had no sin of his own, and he didn't just bring a sacrifice. He became it.
- "he didn't just make the sacrifice for sin, he is the sacrifice for sin."
- "He's both priest and sacrifice."

4. Don't stay a baby: hear it, believe it, obey it, repeat (verses 11-14).
At verse 11 the writer suddenly "goes from preaching and teaching to coaching and admonishing." Pastor Joel joked about scanning in at the gym, sitting in a chair for 30 minutes, and going home. That doesn't build muscle, and just sitting in church doesn't build maturity.
- "We don't become spiritually mature just by hanging around spiritual things."
- "Hear it, believe it, obey it, repeat."
- "I would trade you a million Bible studies where all you do is hear God's Word for just one where you heard it and believed it and obeyed it and did it again."
- "we don't need to keep looking for a more interesting Savior. We just need to start paying real attention to the one we already have."

He closed by making clear this isn't about trying harder: "the same grace that saves us is the same grace that will change us."

TAKEAWAYS FOR OUR MARRIAGE AND FAMILY

- Practice, not just information. "It's the consistent practice of the right things." Small daily habits together, like reading a passage, praying, and talking about it, will grow us more than a big emotional moment once in a while.
- Make it hear, believe, obey at home. When we read something together, let's ask what it would look like to actually do it this week, not just agree with it.
- Jesus gets what we're going through. Whatever stress or hurt either of us is carrying, we can bring it to him, because he says, "I get it."
- Make it personal. "There's a difference between knowing what Jesus did and knowing that He did it for you." Let's help Jordyn see that Jesus did it for her, not just for people in a story.
- Grace, not pressure. We don't grow by pushing each other harder. The same grace that saved us changes us, and that's how we should treat each other too.
- A hopeful note: after the service he mentioned a couple who came to Grace Life in the middle of a divorce, and Jesus has been restoring their marriage. They were reconciling today.

WHAT OTHER TRUSTED TEACHERS SAY

John Piper, "He Is the Source of Eternal Salvation for All Who Obey Him" (sermon on Hebrews 5:4-10, Desiring God)
Piper focuses on verse 5, where God answers the question of Christ's priesthood by calling him "my Son." His point is that only someone with the dignity of God's own Son could win an eternal salvation for us. That matches the sermon's first point: Jesus wasn't just selected by God, he is God's Son.
"No one but the Son of God could do it."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/he-is-the-source-of-eternal-salvation-for-all-who-obey-him

John Piper, "By This Time You Ought to Be Teachers" (sermon on Hebrews 5:11-14, Desiring God)
Piper walks through the warnings in Hebrews (pay attention, consider Jesus, don't harden your hearts) and says verse 11 finally names the root problem. It's the same "dull of hearing" problem the sermon warned about, where we hear about Jesus but it doesn't sink in.
"Here’s the disease he is working on in this letter: dullness of hearing."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/by-this-time-you-ought-to-be-teachers

Tony Evans, "A Simple Test" (devotional on Hebrews 5:12, TonyEvans.org)
Dr. Evans gives a practical test for whether we're "meat" Christians or still on milk: can we actually use God's Word with the people around us? He points out that the "trained" in verse 14 comes from the same root as our word gymnasium, which fits the sermon's gym illustration perfectly.
"...we should be able to explain biblical truths to our children."
https://go.tonyevans.org/blog/a-simple-test

Will Graham, "Are You Growing in Your Faith?" (devotion, Billy Graham Evangelistic Association)
Billy Graham's grandson lists four signs of stalled faith from Hebrews 5:11-14: dull, refusing to grow, unskilled, and not exercising discernment. His remedy is to build on what we already know, be determined to grow, and depend on God for that growth. That lines up with the sermon's "hear it, believe it, obey it, repeat," and its reminder that it's grace that changes us.
"They sat and listened, but were not paying attention and applying what they had learned from God’s Word."
https://billygraham.org/articles/will-graham-devotion-are-you-growing-in-your-faith

Billy Graham Evangelistic Association, "What Does the Bible Mean When It Says Like Newborn Babies, We Should Desire the Milk of the Word?" (Answers)
This answer explains that we all start as spiritual newborns, but God never meant for us to stay that way. It names three things we need to grow: God's Word, prayer, and fellowship with other believers. That's a simple daily plan for the consistency the sermon talked about.
"If any of those—God’s Word, prayer, fellowship—is missing, our growth will be stunted."
https://billygraham.org/answers/what-does-the-bible-mean-when-it-says-like-newborn-babies-we-should-desire-the-milk-of-the-word

Love you,

sermons.subject: Sunday's Sermon at Grace Life: "What a Savior, Part 12: Four Hard Things That Love Sometimes Needs to Say" (Hebrews 6:1-12)
sermons.title: What a Savior, Part 12: Four Hard Things That Love Sometimes Needs to Say
sermons.church: Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
sermons.body:
Hi Sanqueta,

I wanted to share a summary of today's sermon at Grace Life so we can go over it together.

WHAT A SAVIOR, PART 12: FOUR HARD THINGS THAT LOVE SOMETIMES NEEDS TO SAY
Grace Life Baptist Church, McCalla, AL
Sunday, November 8, 2026
Passage: Hebrews 6:1-12
Watch it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P0S9hJnMf5k

"Therefore let us move beyond the elementary teachings about Christ and be taken forward to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from acts that lead to death, and of faith in God, instruction about cleansing rites, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment. And God permitting, we will do so.

It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit, who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age and who have fallen away, to be brought back to repentance. To their loss they are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting him to public disgrace. Land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is farmed receives the blessing of God. But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless and is in danger of being cursed. In the end it will be burned.

Even though we speak like this, dear friends, we are convinced of better things in your case—the things that have to do with salvation. God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown him as you have helped his people and continue to help them. We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, so that what you hope for may be fully realized. We do not want you to become lazy, but to imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised." (Hebrews 6:1-12, NIV)

THE BIG IDEA

The pastor started by asking if we've ever loved someone enough to have a hard conversation with them, even knowing it might not come out right or land right. He said "there are times when love requires a hard conversation," and that's what Hebrews 6 is: a pastor who loves his people too much to sit back and watch them drift away from Jesus. He asked us to picture two people in two chairs at the same church, hearing the same sermons and singing the same songs. Over time one grows closer to Jesus and softer, and the other loses interest in God's Word, God's things and God's people, and grows harder. Before we turn this chapter into a debate, he said, remember that "...the writer's biggest concern is not that we win some kind of theological argument or debate. The writer's concern is that we don't lose this person."

THE MAIN POINTS

He walked through four hard things that love sometimes needs to say.

1. "I want more for you than this." (verses 1-3)
The readers knew the basics of the old covenant (repentance, faith, washings, laying hands on sacrifices, resurrection, judgment), but those were only a foundation pointing to Jesus. They kept re-laying the foundation and never built on it. He compared it to pouring a house foundation, setting a couch on it and calling it home, then pouring it again every year.
- "I want, and God wants, more for you than this."
- "You never graduate the gospel."
- "At some point, you got to build on, right?"
- "You can grow up in church and sit in the chairs and know the stories and be able to sing the songs, all of it, and still never have personally entrusted your life into the hands of Jesus."

2. "I need you to understand how serious this is." (verses 4-8)
Verses 4-6 describe people who were enlightened and saw the truth clearly, then deliberately walked away. Same rain falls on two fields, but one grows a crop and the other grows thorns. He said restoring someone who rejects Jesus is impossible not because grace runs out, but because there's no other Savior to go to. He was clear that this isn't about true believers losing salvation: "once a person is truly saved, they are always saved." He believes these are people who walked right up to the line of salvation and turned away. And he had a word for tender hearts who worry about their own struggles.
- "if you're still asking that question, if that's still concerning you, then you ain't too far gone."
- "struggling is not the same thing as rejecting."
- "Doubting is not the same thing as abandoning..."
- "Same rain, different harvests..."
- "Not because God's grace has limits. It does not."

3. "I see reasons for hope in you." (verses 9-10)
Right after one of the strongest warnings in the Bible, the writer calls them "beloved" and says he's sure of better things for them. The evidence he points to is their love for God shown in serving his people. Love warns, but love also looks for God's fingerprints in people and says so.
- "We ought to be like CSI looking for the grace of God in this world."
- "...love demands that we warn when we need to warn, but love demands that we encourage, we call out good when there's good to be called out."
- "Those good works did not earn their salvation. Those good works proved their salvation."
- "God sees your faithfulness when nobody else does."

4. "I want you to keep going." (verses 11-12)
Love doesn't just pat someone on the shoulder and leave them where they are. "Each of you" is personal, and the examples to imitate are the faithful in Hebrews 11 like Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Rahab, Ruth, Moses and David.
- "You ain't at the end yet. Your eyes are still open. You're still breathing. So keep going."
- "Love does not say, hey, my fingers are crossed. Best of luck, I hope everything works out."
- "If you're encouraged, keep going. If you're discouraged, keep going."

He closed by asking each of us to quietly ask, "What are you saying to me today?" and to pray, "Lord, help me, help me today to trust You and to treasure You supremely." He reminded us from last week that Jesus is our high priest who understands us: "He's not pointing a finger today looking to accuse you of something." Whether we're struggling, ashamed, worn out or tempted to drift, the answer is the same: run to Jesus.

TAKEAWAYS FOR OUR MARRIAGE AND FAMILY

- Hard conversations can be love. He said "some of you are gonna have to go have some hard conversations this week." When one of us sees the other drifting or stuck, saying so gently is love, not criticism. Let's give each other permission to do that.
- Be CSI for grace at home. Let's look for and name what God is doing in each other and in Jordyn, Elijah and Enoch, not just point out what's wrong. Warning and encouraging both belong.
- Our kids need Jesus, not just church. Knowing the songs and stories isn't the same as trusting Jesus personally. Let's keep having real conversations with each of them about where they are with him.
- Struggling isn't rejecting. If one of us or one of the kids is wrestling with a sin or with doubt, that tender, worried heart is a good sign. We can point each other to Jesus our high priest instead of to shame.
- Keep going together. In easy seasons, ask God to help us treasure him more than the blessings. In hard seasons, ask him to help us trust him anyway.
- Something we can do this week: the church is packing Operation Christmas Child shoeboxes. They can be brought to church next Sunday to be prayed over (he said that isn't the final deadline). It could be a good thing to do with the kids.

WHAT OTHER TRUSTED TEACHERS SAY

John Piper, "When Is Saving Repentance Impossible?" (sermon on Hebrews 6:4-8, Desiring God)
Piper says this warning exposes a false sense of security: someone can have real religious experiences and still not be saved, and the point is to make us flee to God and dependence on him. That's the same picture as the sermon's two chairs and the field that drinks the rain but grows thorns.
"And so this text is a warning to us not to assume that we are secure when our lives have some religious experiences but no growing fruit."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/when-is-saving-repentance-impossible

John Piper, "The Full Assurance of Hope to the End" (sermon on Hebrews 6:9-12, Desiring God)
Piper notices that "beloved" in verse 9 is the only time the writer calls them that, right after his hardest words. He shares about taking loved ones to lunch to ask hard questions about their spiritual lives, and how risky that feels. It fits the sermon's whole theme of love being willing to have the hard conversation.
"The writer to the Hebrews is calling us by his example to grow up and to take the risks of love."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-full-assurance-of-hope-to-the-end

John Piper, "Savoring God by Serving the Saints" (sermon on Hebrews 6:9-12, Desiring God)
Piper focuses on verse 10 and how loving God's name shows up in serving his people, without ever replacing love for God himself. It matches the sermon's third point, that God sees our quiet service when nobody else does.
"...God will not forget your work and your love for his name. He will remember."
https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/savoring-god-by-serving-the-saints

Billy Graham Evangelistic Association, "In Christ, we become members of the family of God" (Answers)
Answering someone afraid they might lose their salvation, the answer says a true child of God stays in God's family, like a child stays in their family even when they rebel. It also gives the same warning the sermon did, about assuming we belong to Christ when we don't.
"The first is a warning against false belief — that is, assuming we’re committed to Christ when we really aren’t."
https://billygraham.org/answers/in-christ-we-become-members-of-the-family-of-god

Tony Evans, "Maturity Involves Development" (devotional on Hebrews 5:13-6:1, TonyEvans.org)
Dr. Evans says we have to master the basics but aren't meant to stay there forever, and growth happens when we connect what we learn in Scripture to how we live. That's the sermon's first point about building on the foundation instead of re-pouring it.
"Spiritual growth takes place on the playing field of life, not in the classroom."
https://go.tonyevans.org/blog/maturity-involves-development

Love you,
